name: Technology Department
description: Internal department responsible for enterprise architecture and technology governance at FirstUK Bank. Owns the Business Ontology document and sets standards for data engineering and system design.
context: Audience | Architects, Data Engineers, Domain Experts

name: Enterprise Architect
description: Leadership role responsible for owning and maintaining the FirstUK Bank Business Ontology document. Accountable for enterprise architecture governance and standards alignment.

name: Business Ontology
description: The formal conceptual framework and data model defining core domain entities and their relationships across FirstUK Bank. Serves as the authoritative reference for architects, data engineers, and domain experts. Aligned with FIBO and ISO 20022 standards.
context: Standards Reference | FIBO (Financial Industry Business Ontology), ISO 20022
definition: Structured framework for defining banking concepts, entities, and relationships across FirstUK Bank

name: Document Review Cycle
description: Annual review schedule for the Business Ontology document, establishing governance cadence and update accountability.
what_it_measures: Frequency of business ontology document review and update

name: FirstUK Bank
description: The primary banking organization whose enterprise ontology, core concepts, entities, relationships, and constraints are defined in this document. FirstUK Bank operates across multiple business domains with a shared semantic understanding.
context: The Business Ontology defines the core concepts, entities, relationships, and constraints that govern FirstUK Bank's enterprise.
mission: Core banking enterprise governed by a business ontology that defines concepts, entities, relationships, and constraints across business domains

name: Business Ontology
description: The formal definition of core concepts, entities, relationships, and constraints that govern FirstUK Bank's enterprise. It provides a shared semantic understanding of business domains, enabling effective knowledge representation, data integration, and enterprise reasoning.
context: The Business Ontology defines the core concepts, entities, relationships, and constraints that govern FirstUK Bank's enterprise.
It provides a shared semantic understanding of business domains, enabling effective knowledge representation, data integration, and enterprise reasoning.
definition: The core concepts, entities, relationships, and constraints that govern FirstUK Bank's enterprise
business_rules: Provides shared semantic understanding across the organization
Enables effective data integration
Supports enterprise-wide reasoning

name: Entities Defined Count
description: The quantitative measure of the number of core entities defined within the Business Ontology.
what_it_measures: Number of core entities defined in the Business Ontology

name: Relationships Defined Count
description: The quantitative measure of the number of relationships defined within the Business Ontology.
what_it_measures: Number of relationships defined in the Business Ontology

name: Constraints Defined Count
description: The quantitative measure of the number of constraints defined within the Business Ontology.
what_it_measures: Number of constraints defined in the Business Ontology

name: Ontology
description: The foundational conceptual framework that defines how FirstUK Bank structures and understands its business entities, processes, and relationships. The ontology is built on five core principles: realism, consistency, completeness, clarity, and traceability.
context: Concepts map to real-world business entities
Concepts maintain consistent definitions across documents
Concepts link to policies, procedures, and systems
definition: A structured framework of banking concepts that map to real-world business entities and maintain consistent definitions across documents

name: Realism Principle
description: A foundational ontology principle requiring that all concepts defined in the FirstUK Bank business ontology must map to real-world business entities, ensuring the conceptual model reflects actual banking operations and structures.
context: Realism: Concepts map to real-world business entities
rule_statement: Concepts must map to real-world business entities

name: Consistency Principle
description: A foundational ontology principle requiring that concepts maintain consistent definitions across all FirstUK Bank documents, preventing ambiguity and ensuring unified understanding of business entities throughout the organization.
context: Consistency: Concepts maintain consistent definitions across documents
rule_statement: Concepts must maintain consistent definitions across documents

name: Completeness Principle
description: A foundational ontology principle requiring that all critical business concepts relevant to FirstUK Bank operations are defined within the ontology, ensuring no essential banking entities or processes are omitted.
context: Completeness: Critical business concepts are defined
rule_statement: Critical business concepts must be defined within the ontology

name: Clarity Principle
description: A foundational ontology principle requiring that all concept definitions within the FirstUK Bank ontology are unambiguous and precise, enabling consistent interpretation and application across the organization.
context: Clarity: Definitions are unambiguous and precise
rule_statement: Definitions must be unambiguous and precise

name: Traceability Principle
description: A foundational ontology principle requiring that all concepts defined in the FirstUK Bank ontology link to supporting policies, procedures, and systems, establishing clear accountability and operational grounding for each conceptual entity.
context: Traceability: Concepts link to policies, procedures, and systems
rule_statement: Concepts must link to policies, procedures, and systems

name: Party
description: A foundational domain entity representing people and organizations that interact with the bank. Parties form the basis of the Party & Customer Domain within FirstUK Bank's business ontology.
context: Party & Customer Domain — People and organizations interacting with the bank
definition: People and organizations interacting with the bank

name: Customer
description: A core domain entity within the Party & Customer Domain representing individuals or entities that hold banking relationships with FirstUK Bank. Customers are central to account, product, and transaction management.
context: Party & Customer Domain — People and organizations interacting with the bank
definition: People and organizations interacting with the bank

name: Product
description: A core domain entity representing banking products and services offered by FirstUK Bank. Products form the conceptual foundation of the Product Domain.
context: Product Domain — Banking products and services
definition: Banking products and services

name: Account
description: A core domain entity representing customer accounts and holdings within FirstUK Bank. Accounts are the primary vehicle through which customers interact with banking products and services.
context: Account Domain — Customer accounts and holdings
definition: Customer accounts and holdings

name: Transaction
description: A core domain entity representing money movement and account activity. Transactions capture all financial events occurring on customer accounts within FirstUK Bank.
context: Transaction Domain — Money movement and account activity
definition: Money movement and account activity

name: Risk & Compliance Concept
description: A foundational domain entity encompassing regulatory and risk concepts that govern FirstUK Bank's operations. This domain includes AML screening, KYC verification, SAR filing, and fraud detection obligations.
context: Risk & Compliance Domain — Regulatory and risk concepts
definition: Regulatory and risk concepts

name: Organization
description: The organizational structure and roles domain within FirstUK Bank's business ontology. This domain defines how the bank is structured and how roles and responsibilities are distributed.
context: Organization Domain — Organizational structure and roles
mission: Banking organization providing products and services to customers

name: Party
description: Any natural person or organization that interacts with FirstUK Bank. Parties are classified by type (individual, organization, employee, or regulatory authority) and tracked with unique identifiers and registration dates.
context: Any natural person or organization that interacts with FirstUK Bank.
Subtypes: Natural Person (individual customer), Organization (business customer, future), Employee, Regulatory Authority
Key Attributes: party_id — Unique identifier, party_type — Type of party (individual, organization), name — Full legal name, registration_date — Date party entered relationship with bank
definition: Any natural person or organization that interacts with FirstUK Bank

name: Natural Person
description: A natural person subtype of Party representing an individual customer who interacts with FirstUK Bank.
definition: Individual customer

name: Organization
description: An organization subtype of Party representing a business customer or future business customer of FirstUK Bank.
definition: Business customer

name: Employee
description: An employee subtype of Party representing FirstUK Bank staff members who interact with the bank's systems and customers.
definition: Bank employee

name: Regulatory Authority
description: A regulatory authority subtype of Party representing government and regulatory bodies that interact with FirstUK Bank.
definition: Regulatory body that interacts with FirstUK Bank

name: Customer
description: A natural person who holds at least one account with FirstUK Bank. Customers are identified by unique customer_id and must complete KYC verification and AML screening before account opening. Each customer can hold multiple accounts and may participate in joint account arrangements.
context: A natural person (individual) who holds at least one account with FirstUK Bank
Every customer must have a valid identity (see KYC concept)
Every customer must pass AML screening before account opening
definition: A natural person (individual) who holds at least one account with FirstUK Bank
business_rules: Every customer must have a valid identity
Every customer must pass AML screening before account opening
Customer can hold multiple accounts
Customer can have joint account holders

name: Account
description: A banking account held by a customer with FirstUK Bank. Accounts are linked to customers through a one-to-many relationship and form the primary vehicle for customer banking relationships.
context: A natural person (individual) who holds at least one account with FirstUK Bank
definition: A financial account held by a customer with FirstUK Bank

name: KYC Verification
description: The Know Your Customer identity verification process required for all customers before account opening. KYC verification is a mandatory compliance obligation and is linked to customers on a one-to-many basis to support periodic refresh and enhanced due diligence.
context: Every customer must have a valid identity (see KYC concept)
definition: Know Your Customer verification process to establish and verify customer identity
business_rules: Every customer must have a valid identity
regulatory_significance: Required for customer onboarding and ongoing compliance

name: AML Screening
description: Anti-Money Laundering screening that must be completed for every customer before account opening. AML screening is a mandatory regulatory obligation to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
context: Every customer must pass AML screening before account opening
definition: Anti-Money Laundering screening process to assess customer risk and detect suspicious activity
business_rules: Every customer must pass AML screening before account opening
regulatory_significance: Mandatory compliance requirement for financial institutions

name: Address
description: The registered address associated with a customer. Customers can have multiple addresses linked to their profile for KYC and compliance purposes.
definition: Registered address information associated with a customer

name: Party
description: The foundational entity representing a natural or legal person in the FirstUK Bank system. Customer identifiers are linked to Party records for unified identity management.
definition: A legal entity or natural person that can hold accounts and enter into banking relationships

name: Customer Identity Requirement
description: A mandatory business rule requiring every customer to have a valid identity verified through the KYC process before or during their relationship with FirstUK Bank.
context: Every customer must have a valid identity (see KYC concept)
rule_statement: Every customer must have a valid identity established through KYC verification
consequence: Customer cannot open or maintain accounts without valid identity verification

name: Customer AML Screening Requirement
description: A mandatory business rule requiring every customer to pass AML screening before account opening. This is a regulatory obligation to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
context: Every customer must pass AML screening before account opening
rule_statement: Every customer must pass AML screening before account opening
consequence: Account opening is blocked if customer fails AML screening

name: Multiple Account Holding
description: A business rule permitting customers to hold multiple accounts simultaneously with FirstUK Bank, enabling diverse product holdings and account arrangements.
rule_statement: A customer can hold multiple accounts with FirstUK Bank

name: Joint Account Holder Permission
description: A business rule permitting customers to participate as joint account holders on accounts with other customers, enabling shared account arrangements.
context: Customer can have joint account holders
rule_statement: A customer can have joint account holders on their accounts

name: Address
description: Physical location associated with a customer, account, or branch. Addresses are classified by type (Registered, Correspondence, or Branch) and must comply with UK postcode formatting requirements. Address verification through utility bills or council tax documentation is a mandatory control for UK customers.
context: Physical location associated with a customer, account, or branch.
UK customers must have a UK address
Address must be verified (utility bill, council tax, etc.)
definition: Physical location associated with a customer, account, or branch
business_rule: UK customers must have a UK address

name: Address Verification
description: Mandatory control requiring that all customer addresses be verified using acceptable documentation such as utility bills or council tax records before account activation or use.
context: Address must be verified (utility bill, council tax, etc.)
rule_statement: Address must be verified using acceptable documentation

name: UK Address Requirement for UK Customers
canonical_name: UK Address Requirement for UK Customers
description: Regulatory constraint mandating that all UK-based customers maintain a registered address within the United Kingdom.
context: UK customers must have a UK address
rule_statement: UK customers must have a UK address

name: UK Postcode Format Compliance
description: Technical constraint requiring that all UK postcodes conform to the standard UK postcode format: A(1,2)9(1,2)A 9A(2), where A represents letters and 9 represents digits.
rule_statement: Addresses must use UK postcode format: A(1,2)9(1,2)A 9A(2)

name: Identification Document
description: Official document used to verify customer identity as part of KYC compliance. Captures unique identifiers, document type, issuing country, and verification status throughout the customer lifecycle.
context: Official document used to verify customer identity (KYC)
doc_type — Passport, Driving License, ID Card
definition: Official document used to verify customer identity (KYC)
business_rules: Document must be official and issued by recognized authority
Verification status must be tracked (Unverified, Verified, Expired, Rejected)
regulatory_significance: Core component of KYC (Know Your Customer) compliance requirements

name: KYC Verification
description: The identity verification process using official identification documents as part of customer due diligence obligations. Encompasses document collection, validation, and status tracking.
context: Official document used to verify customer identity (KYC)
Accepted Types (UK): UK Passport, UK Driving License, UK National ID Card (future)
definition: Process of verifying customer identity using official identification documents
business_rules: Identification documents must be from accepted types
Documents must not be expired
Verification status must be tracked and maintained
regulatory_significance: Mandatory compliance requirement for customer onboarding and ongoing account management

name: UK Passport
description: Accepted UK identification document type for KYC verification purposes.
context: Accepted Types (UK): UK Passport, UK Driving License, UK National ID Card (future)
definition: Official travel and identification document issued by the UK government
business_rules: Must be current and not expired for verification purposes
Issued by UK authority
regulatory_significance: Accepted form of identification for KYC verification in UK banking

name: UK Driving License
description: Accepted UK identification document type for KYC verification purposes.
context: Accepted Types (UK): UK Passport, UK Driving License, UK National ID Card (future)
definition: Official driving authorization document issued by DVLA that serves as identification
business_rules: Must be current and not expired for verification purposes
Issued by UK authority
regulatory_significance: Accepted form of identification for KYC verification in UK banking

name: UK National ID Card
description: Planned future accepted UK identification document type for KYC verification purposes.
context: Accepted Types (UK): UK Passport, UK Driving License, UK National ID Card (future)
definition: Official national identification card issued by the UK government
business_rules: Must be current and not expired for verification purposes
Issued by UK authority
regulatory_significance: Accepted form of identification for KYC verification in UK banking (future implementation noted)

name: Product
description: A financial service offered by FirstUK Bank, characterized by a unique product identifier, marketing name, product type classification, and associated features and pricing tiers. Products are defined by their launch status, balance requirements, and target customer segments.
context: A financial service offered by FirstUK Bank
definition: A financial service offered by FirstUK Bank

name: Feature
description: A capability or characteristic associated with a Product, linked through a one-to-many relationship. Features define the functional offerings available within a product.
definition: A capability or characteristic of a Product

name: Pricing Tier
description: A pricing structure variant associated with a Product, linked through a one-to-many relationship. Pricing tiers define different rate or fee levels available within a product.
definition: A pricing structure variant associated with a Product

name: SmartSaver Account
description: A savings product offered by FirstUK Bank with a minimum opening balance of £1, targeted at general consumers aged 18 and above. The account is identified by product_id SAV-001 and represents an active savings offering.

name: Minimum Opening Balance
description: The minimum balance required to open a SmartSaver Account, set at £1. This represents the entry-level capital requirement for account activation.
what_it_measures: Minimum balance required to open a SmartSaver Account

name: Feature
description: A specific capability or service included in a banking product. Features define the functional offerings available to customers and are associated with one or more products with defined effective dates.
context: A specific capability or service included in a product.
definition: A specific capability or service included in a product

name: Easy Access
description: A product feature that permits withdrawals without notice, providing customers with immediate liquidity on their accounts.
definition: Withdrawals without notice

name: Interest Accrual
description: A product feature that accrues interest on account balances, offered on either a variable or fixed rate basis.
definition: Variable or fixed interest calculation and accumulation

name: Online Banking
description: A product feature providing customers with web-based access to manage their accounts and conduct transactions.
definition: Digital banking capability accessible via web platform

name: Mobile App
description: A product feature providing customers with mobile application access to manage their accounts and conduct transactions.
definition: Mobile application for banking services

name: Debit Card
description: A payment card feature included in products, enabling customers to make purchases and withdraw cash at point of sale and ATMs.

name: Standing Order
description: A product feature enabling customers to set up recurring payment instructions on their accounts.
definition: Recurring payment instruction set up by customer

name: Direct Debit
description: A product feature enabling customers to authorize third parties to collect variable or fixed payments from their accounts.
definition: Automated payment collection mechanism

name: Joint Account Support
description: A product feature enabling multiple customers to hold and manage an account jointly with shared rights and liabilities.
definition: Capability to hold and manage accounts with multiple account holders

name: Interest Rate
description: A specific rate of interest applied to accounts, defined by rate type, tier structure, and review basis. Interest rates can be fixed, variable, or tiered, with each tier linked to a balance threshold and annual percentage value. Rates are subject to periodic review based on external factors such as Bank of England base rate movements.
context: A specific rate of interest applied to accounts.
review_basis — Linked to Bank of England base rate, margin
definition: A specific rate of interest applied to accounts
business_rules: Tiered rates apply based on balance thresholds
Rates linked to Bank of England base rate with margin adjustment
Subject to periodic review on planned dates

name: Tier 1 Interest Rate
description: The interest rate applied to balances within the first tier threshold of £0–£10,000 on a tiered variable savings product, set at 4.5% AER effective 2026-01-15.
what_it_measures: Annual equivalent rate (AER) for balance tier £0–£10,000

name: Tier 2 Interest Rate
description: The interest rate applied to balances within the second tier threshold of £10,001–£50,000 on a tiered variable savings product, set at 4.7% AER effective 2026-01-15.
what_it_measures: Annual equivalent rate (AER) for balance tier £10,001–£50,000

name: Tier 3 Interest Rate
description: The interest rate applied to balances within the third tier threshold of £50,001 and above on a tiered variable savings product, set at 4.8% AER effective 2026-01-15.
what_it_measures: Annual equivalent rate (AER) for balance tier £50,001+

name: Interest Rate Review Basis
description: The interest rate on the tiered variable savings product is linked to the Bank of England base rate plus a fixed margin of 2.5%, establishing the mechanism by which rates are adjusted in response to external monetary policy changes.
context: review_basis — Linked to Bank of England base rate, margin
rule_statement: Interest rates are reviewed and adjusted based on Bank of England base rate movements plus a fixed margin of 2.5%
regulatory_source: Bank of England monetary policy framework

name: Account
description: A contractual arrangement between a customer and FirstUK Bank to hold money, make transactions, and earn interest. Accounts are uniquely identified and linked to a primary customer, a product, and a transaction ledger. Each account maintains a status (Active, Dormant, Closed, or Suspended) and tracks both current and available balances.
context: A contractual arrangement between a customer and FirstUK Bank to hold money, make transactions, and earn interest.
Every account must have one primary account holder (customer)
Account balance is calculated from transaction ledger
Account can only be in one status at a time
definition: A contractual arrangement between a customer and FirstUK Bank to hold money, make transactions, and earn interest
business_rule: Every account must have one primary account holder
Account balance is calculated from transaction ledger
Account can only be in one status at a time

name: Customer
description: A natural person who holds a contractual arrangement with FirstUK Bank. Each customer serves as the primary account holder and is uniquely identified with a customer_id that links to one or more accounts.
context: customer_id — Primary account holder (links to Customer)
Every account must have one primary account holder (customer)
definition: An entity that holds an account with FirstUK Bank and serves as the primary account holder

name: Account Holder
description: A person with legal rights and obligations over an account, including primary holders and joint holders. Account holders are linked to accounts in a one-to-many relationship, allowing for joint account arrangements.
context: Every account must have one primary account holder (customer)
definition: A party with rights and obligations over an account, including primary and joint holders

name: Product
description: A banking product offering linked to an account, such as a savings or current account product. Each account is associated with exactly one product that defines the terms and features available to the account holder.
definition: A banking product offering linked to an account

name: Transaction
description: A financial event on a customer account such as a deposit, withdrawal, transfer, or payment. Transactions are recorded in a ledger and used to calculate the account balance.
context: Account balance is calculated from transaction ledger
definition: A financial movement of funds on an account
business_rule: Account balance is calculated from transaction ledger

name: Standing Order
description: A standing order payment instruction set up on a customer account. Multiple standing orders can be associated with a single account.
definition: A recurring transaction instruction set up on an account

name: Card
description: A payment card issued in connection with a customer account. Multiple cards can be linked to a single account.
definition: A payment card linked to an account

name: Primary Account Holder Requirement
description: A mandatory constraint requiring that every account must have exactly one primary account holder (customer). This establishes the foundational accountability relationship for the account.
context: Every account must have one primary account holder (customer)
rule_statement: Every account must have one primary account holder
regulatory_significance: Establishes clear ownership and accountability for account management

name: Account Balance Calculation Rule
description: A rule governing that account balance is calculated from the transaction ledger, ensuring that the balance is always derived from recorded transactions rather than stored independently.
context: Account balance is calculated from transaction ledger
rule_statement: Account balance is calculated from transaction ledger
regulatory_significance: Ensures accurate and auditable balance reporting

name: Account Status Exclusivity Rule
description: A constraint requiring that an account can only be in one status at a time. Valid statuses are Active, Dormant, Closed, or Suspended.
context: Account can only be in one status at a time
rule_statement: Account can only be in one status at a time
regulatory_significance: Prevents ambiguous account state and ensures clear operational status

name: Closed Account Non-Reactivation Rule
description: A constraint establishing that closed accounts are not reactivated, ensuring finality once an account is closed.
rule_statement: Closed accounts are not reactivated
regulatory_significance: Prevents unauthorized reactivation of terminated accounts and maintains audit trail integrity

name: Account Holder
description: A person with legal rights and responsibilities for an account, including primary, joint, and secondary holders. Account holders have defined signatory authority, KYC/AML obligations, and liability for account activities such as overdrafts.
context: A person with legal rights and responsibilities for an account.
Account must have at least one primary holder
Joint account: Both holders must pass KYC/AML
Either can withdraw, both liable for overdraft
definition: A person with legal rights and responsibilities for an account
business_rules: Account must have at least one primary holder
Joint account: Both holders must pass KYC/AML
Either joint holder can withdraw full balance
Interest calculated on total balance (not per holder)

name: Account Holder Primary Requirement
description: Every account must have at least one primary holder with full legal rights and responsibilities.
context: Account must have at least one primary holder
rule_statement: Account must have at least one primary holder

name: Joint Account KYC/AML Requirement
description: Both holders on a joint account must pass KYC and AML screening before the account can be activated or used.
context: Joint account: Both holders must pass KYC/AML
rule_statement: Both holders must pass KYC/AML verification
regulatory_significance: Compliance with KYC and AML regulations

name: Joint Account Withdrawal Authority
description: Either joint holder on an account has the authority to withdraw the full balance without requiring consent from the other holder.
context: Either joint holder can withdraw full balance
Either can withdraw, both liable for overdraft
rule_statement: Either joint holder can withdraw the full balance

name: Joint Account Interest Calculation
description: Interest on a joint account is calculated on the total balance held in the account, not separately per holder.
context: Interest calculated on total balance (not per holder)
rule_statement: Interest calculated on total balance, not per holder

name: Joint Account Overdraft Liability
description: Both joint holders are jointly and severally liable for any overdraft on the account, regardless of which holder initiated the overdraft.
rule_statement: Both holders are liable for overdraft

name: Joint Account ACC-00002
description: A joint account held by John Smith and Jane Smith with shared withdrawal rights and joint liability for overdrafts.

name: John Smith Primary Holder
description: Primary holder of joint account ACC-00002 with full legal rights and responsibilities, linked to customer CUST-00002.

name: Jane Smith Joint Holder
description: Joint holder of account ACC-00002 with equal withdrawal authority and joint liability, linked to customer CUST-00003.
liability_scope: Joint and several liability for overdraft

name: John Smith
description: Individual customer holding primary holder status on joint account ACC-00002.
context_role: Primary holder of joint account ACC-00002

name: Jane Smith
description: Individual customer holding joint holder status on joint account ACC-00002.
context_role: Joint holder of joint account ACC-00002

name: KYC Verification
description: Compliance obligation requiring verification of account holder identity and eligibility before account activation, particularly mandatory for joint account holders.
context: Joint account: Both holders must pass KYC/AML
definition: Process to verify the identity and legitimacy of account holders
regulatory_significance: Required for both holders in joint accounts as part of compliance obligations

name: AML Screening
description: Compliance obligation requiring screening of account holders against sanctions and PEP lists before account activation, particularly mandatory for joint account holders.
context: Joint account: Both holders must pass KYC/AML
definition: Process to screen account holders against sanctions and adverse lists
regulatory_significance: Required for both holders in joint accounts as part of compliance obligations

name: Joint Account
description: An account held by two or more customers with joint and several liability. Both account holders share equal responsibility for overdrafts and can independently initiate transactions. Interest allocation and dispute resolution are governed by defined business rules and complaint handling procedures.
context: An account held by two or more customers with joint and several liability.
Both holders must consent to account closure
definition: An account held by two or more customers with joint and several liability
business_rules: Both holders must consent to account closure
Both holders responsible for overdraft
Both holders can initiate transactions
Dispute resolution per Complaint Handling procedures
regulatory_significance: Both holders jointly and severally liable; both included in AML due diligence; both entitled to account information

name: Account Holder
description: A party with legal rights and obligations over a joint account. Joint account holders are jointly and severally liable for account activity, must consent to account closure, and are both entitled to account information and included in AML due diligence.
context: Both holders must consent to account closure
Both holders jointly and severally liable
Both included in AML due diligence
due_diligence_requirement: Both holders included in AML due diligence

name: Joint and Several Liability
description: A legal arrangement where both account holders are individually and collectively responsible for all account obligations, including overdrafts and account closure decisions.
context: Joint and Several, Tenants in Common
Both holders jointly and severally liable
definition: Legal arrangement where each account holder is individually and collectively responsible for the full account balance and obligations
business_rules: Both holders responsible for overdraft
Each holder liable for full account balance
regulatory_significance: Both holders jointly and severally liable under banking regulations

name: Joint Account Closure Consent Requirement
description: A governance rule requiring that both holders of a joint account must provide explicit consent before the account can be closed.
context: Both holders must consent to account closure
rule_statement: Both holders must consent to account closure

name: Joint Account Overdraft Liability
description: A constraint establishing that both holders of a joint account are jointly and severally responsible for any overdraft on the account.
rule_statement: Both holders are responsible for overdraft

name: Joint Account Transaction Authority
description: An operational rule permitting either holder of a joint account to independently initiate transactions without requiring consent from the other holder.
rule_statement: Both holders can initiate transactions

name: Joint Account AML Due Diligence
description: A regulatory requirement that both holders of a joint account must be included in Anti-Money Laundering due diligence procedures.
context: Both included in AML due diligence
rule_statement: Both holders must be included in AML due diligence

name: Joint Account Information Access
description: A regulatory obligation ensuring that both holders of a joint account are entitled to receive and access all account information.
rule_statement: Both holders are entitled to account information
regulatory_source: Banking regulations and data access rights

name: Interest Split
description: A configurable attribute of a joint account that determines how accrued interest is allocated between account holders, either equally or according to specified percentages.
definition: Method of allocating interest earned on a joint account between account holders

name: Joint Account Dispute Resolution
description: The process by which disputes on a joint account are handled, governed by the bank's Complaint Handling procedures and applicable to both account holders.
definition: Process for resolving disputes on joint accounts
business_rules: Dispute resolution per Complaint Handling procedures

name: Card
description: A payment card (debit, credit, or prepaid) linked to a customer account. Cards are issued with unique identifiers, cardholder names, expiry dates, and security codes. Card status can transition through Active, Inactive, Lost, Stolen, Expired, or Blocked states, with operational rules governing locking, replacement, and transaction limits.
context: A payment card (debit, credit, or prepaid) linked to an account.
Card can be locked/unlocked by cardholder
definition: A payment card (debit, credit, or prepaid) linked to an account
business_rules: Card can be locked/unlocked by cardholder
Lost/stolen cards can be replaced with £15 fee
Only one card per account initially
Contactless limit: £100 per transaction

name: Card Identifier
description: Unique identifier assigned to each payment card for tracking and operational purposes.
definition: Unique identifier for a payment card
business_rules: Uniquely identifies a card within the system

name: Card Number
description: 16-digit card number masked in logs for security purposes. This is the primary identifier used in payment transactions.
definition: 16-digit card number used for payment transactions
business_rules: 16-digit format
Masked in logs for security

name: Card Status
description: The operational state of a card, which can be Active, Inactive, Lost, Stolen, Expired, or Blocked. Status transitions are triggered by cardholder actions, fraud events, or expiration.
context: `card_status` — Active, Inactive, Lost, Stolen, Expired, Blocked
definition: Current operational state of a payment card

name: Card Lock/Unlock Authority
description: Cardholder has the authority to lock and unlock their own card without requiring bank intervention.
context: Card can be locked/unlocked by cardholder
rule_statement: Card can be locked/unlocked by cardholder

name: Card Replacement Fee
description: A fee of £15 is charged when a lost or stolen card is replaced.
rule_statement: Lost or stolen cards can be replaced with a fee of £15

name: Single Card Per Account Constraint
description: Initially, only one card can be issued per account. This constraint may be relaxed for supplementary or replacement cards.
rule_statement: Only one card per account initially

name: Contactless Transaction Limit
description: Contactless card transactions are limited to £100 per transaction.
rule_statement: Contactless transactions are limited to £100 per transaction

name: Daily ATM Transaction Limit
description: The maximum amount a cardholder can withdraw from an ATM in a single day.
what_it_measures: Maximum daily transaction limit for ATM withdrawals

name: Transaction
description: A financial event representing money movement or activity on an account. description: A natural person subject to identity verification, AML screening, address validation, and age requirements as defined in the customer constraints table. The customer must meet all four mandatory constraints before account opening or transaction processing.
definition: An entity that must satisfy identity verification, AML screening, address verification, and minimum age requirements to be eligible for banking services
business_rules: Must have identity verified
Must pass AML screening
Must have valid address
Must be age 18 or older

name: Identity Verification
description: A mandatory compliance control requiring that a customer's identity be verified before account opening or transaction processing. The verification status is tracked as a boolean constraint in the customer record.
consequence_of_failure: customer cannot be onboarded; kyc_status will not be 'Verified'

name: AML Screening
description: A mandatory anti-money laundering control requiring that a customer pass AML screening before account opening or transaction processing. Customers with a flagged AML status are rejected.
hit_or_match_response: customer marked as 'Flagged'; customer fails AML screening requirement

name: Address Verification
description: A mandatory compliance control requiring that a customer have a valid, verified address on file before account opening or transaction processing. The address must be non-null and marked as verified.
context: customer.address IS NOT NULL AND verified
consequence_of_failure: customer cannot be onboarded; address requirement not satisfied

name: Minimum Age Requirement
description: A regulatory constraint requiring that customers be at least 18 years of age to open an account or conduct transactions with the bank.
rule_statement: Customer must be age 18 or older

name: Transaction
description: A financial event on a customer account subject to constraints governing amount validation, account existence, and post-posting immutability. Transactions progress through Pending and Completed states with edit restrictions once posted.
definition: A financial movement of funds between accounts or into/out of an account, characterized by an amount, account reference, and posting status
business_rules: Amount must be greater than zero
Account reference must exist and be valid
Transaction becomes immutable once posted to Completed status

name: Transaction Amount Validation
description: A hard constraint requiring that all transaction amounts must be positive values greater than zero.
rule_statement: Transaction amount must be greater than zero
consequence: Transaction rejected if amount is zero or negative

name: Transaction Account Reference Requirement
description: A referential integrity constraint requiring that every transaction must reference an existing account record in the account table.
rule_statement: Every transaction must reference an existing account via account_id foreign key
consequence: Transaction cannot be created or posted without valid account reference

name: Transaction Post-Posting Immutability
description: A control constraint that prevents editing of completed transactions. Transactions in Pending or Completed status are subject to an edit restriction once posted.
rule_statement: Transactions with Completed status cannot be edited or modified
enforcement: System prevents modification of Completed transactions
consequence: Completed transactions are locked from further amendment; reversal or correction requires new transaction

name: Account
description: A customer account entity that serves as the target reference for all transactions. Accounts are identified by account_id and must exist prior to transaction posting.
definition: A financial holding entity that serves as the target or source for transactions, identified by account_id
business_rules: Account must exist before a transaction can reference it
Account is the mandatory anchor point for all transaction activity

name: SAR Filing Deadline
description: A regulatory constraint requiring that a Suspicious Activity Report must be filed within 30 days of the date suspicion arises. This is a hard compliance deadline enforced across all SAR filings.
rule_statement: Suspicious Activity Report must be filed within 30 days of suspicion date

name: KYC Periodic Refresh Requirement
description: A compliance constraint mandating that Know Your Customer verification must be refreshed within a 3-5 year cycle. The next review date must not exceed 5 years from the current date.
rule_statement: Know Your Customer verification must be refreshed within 3-5 years

name: Fraud Reimbursement Timeline
description: A compliance constraint requiring that fraud-related customer reimbursements must be processed within 10 days of the claim date. This establishes the maximum permissible processing window for fraud compensation.
rule_statement: Fraud claim reimbursement must be processed within 10 days of claim date

name: Suspicious Activity Report
description: A formal report filed to regulatory authorities documenting suspicious customer activity or transactions that may indicate money laundering or other financial crime. Subject to a 30-day filing deadline from the date of suspicion.
definition: A report filed when suspicious activity is detected, requiring submission within 30 days of suspicion
business_rules: Must be filed within 30 days of suspicion date
regulatory_significance: FCA-mandated reporting obligation for financial crime detection

name: Know Your Customer Verification
description: The identity and address verification process required for customer due diligence, subject to periodic refresh requirements every 3-5 years to maintain compliance with regulatory obligations.
definition: Customer identity and background verification process that must be refreshed periodically
business_rules: Must be refreshed within 3-5 years
regulatory_significance: FCA-mandated customer due diligence requirement

name: Fraud Claim
description: A customer claim for reimbursement following a fraud event, subject to a 10-day processing and reimbursement deadline from the date the claim is filed.
definition: A customer claim for reimbursement of fraudulent transactions, requiring processing within 10 days
business_rules: Reimbursement must be processed within 10 days of claim date
regulatory_significance: FCA-mandated consumer protection requirement for fraud liability
